section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Coordinate Systems as Languages
section_1.content: Define a basis as a 'coordinate system'. Just as a point (3, 2) in standard 2D space relies on units (1,0) and (0,1), changing the basis means changing the 'grid lines' of our world. Visualize this as switching from a square grid to a skewed grid.
section_1.example: Imagine a cat sitting on a map. If you use a grid of meters, it's at (2, 3). If you use a grid of 'cat-steps', its position (2, 3) changes to (1, 1). The cat didn't move; our language for describing its position did.

section_2.title: Defining the Transition Matrix
section_2.content: Introduce the Change of Basis Matrix (P). P is constructed by taking the vectors of the 'New Basis' (B') and expressing them in terms of the 'Old Basis' (B). Mathematically, [v]_B = P * [v]_B'.
section_2.example: Visualize two sets of arrows. Set A (standard) and Set B (new, longer, rotated arrows). Draw P as the bridge that takes the coordinates from the Set B world and maps them back to the Set A world.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: How to Calculate
section_3.content: Break down the algorithm: 1. Identify Basis B and B'. 2. Write B' vectors as columns of P. 3. Multiply P by your coordinate vector to 'translate' your point into the standard basis.
section_3.example: A robot arm needs to pick up a toy. The internal sensor uses 'Robot-Basis'. The table uses 'World-Basis'. By multiplying the Robot-Basis vector by P, the robot calculates the correct coordinates to reach the toy in the World-Basis.

section_4.title: Summary & Geometric Intuition
section_4.content: Reiterate that a change of basis is a 'relabelling' of space. The vector remains the same; only its representation in the column vector format changes. Emphasize that P^-1 allows you to go in reverse (from Standard to New Basis).
section_4.example: Show a side-by-side animation: On the left, a point stays fixed while the coordinate axes rotate. On the right, the coordinate values (x, y) update in real-time as the axes transform.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0) # Hide initially per B041

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Transition Matrix", [
            "Transition matrix P maps bases.", 
            "Columns of P are new basis vectors.", 
            "[v]_B = P * [v]_B' relates coordinates."
        ])
        self.lecture.set_opacity(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw vectors v_A and v_B in #FFFFFF
        vA = Vector([1, 1.5], color=WHITE)
        vB = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(vA, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(vB, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(vA), Create(vB))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight basis vectors of system A in #FFFF00
        basisA1 = Vector([1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        basisA2 = Vector([0, 1], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(basisA1, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(basisA2, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(basisA1), Create(basisA2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show projection of v_A onto B basis in #00FF00

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(proj))
        self.wait(2)
